_comment: CryoLean v4 shared property vocabulary for the 20-industry expansion. Written by the vocabulary designer agent. Proposal only: data/capability_vocabulary.json is NOT modified; the integrator adds new_keys there. Experiment ideas are candidates with one real source each; profile authors must re-read the source and quote values verbatim before writing requirements.
decision_semantics: Lean decides a pair when every mandatory requirement key has trusted data. A documented absence (install=not_available with trusted evidence) passes 'absent' constraints and FAILS every other constraint, so documenting absences turns NEED_MORE_INFORMATION into DOES_NOT_MEET. range-shaped capabilities accept point_within/range_within/at_least/at_most; max accepts at_least; min accepts at_most; flag accepts present/absent/flag_is; count accepts count_*; set accepts set_contains.

core_passport.why: The single most discriminating property in all 20 industries: every machine holds its sample/product/test article between a documented lowest and highest temperature (DR mixing-chamber plate, PPMS sample chamber, freezer cabinet set-point range, LN2 dewar storage space e.g. -196 C liquid to -190 C top box, freeze-dryer shelf, TVAC platen/test-article interface, microtome specimen head, probe-station chuck, Stirling cold tip). Experiments use point_within / range_within / at_most / at_least on it, so one documented range decides most pairs, and a documented range that excludes the needed temperature yields DOES_NOT_MEET immediately. Already documented on 25/26 configurations.
core_passport.how_to_document: Range of the SAMPLE position as the manufacturer states it. If only a single storage/operating temperature is stated (e.g. LN2 liquid phase -196 C), use lo = hi = that value. Convert Celsius exactly (T[mK] = (C + 273.15) x 1000).

core_passport.why: Lowest documented temperature; the existing mK experiments (transmon, vector-field transport, wiring heat budget) are written as temperature.base at_most X. Every machine has a lowest temperature, so it is always documentable; keeping it lets the existing quantum profiles decide against new machines (e.g. a -80 C freezer immediately fails 'base <= 20 mK').
core_passport.how_to_document: Equal to temperature.range.lo from the same source unless the source states a separate (lower) base temperature.

core_passport.why: Field is a hard requirement in magnetometry, quantum transport, NMR/MRI, conductor testing and DNP; for the majority of new machines (freezers, dewars, freeze dryers, TVAC, cryocoolers) the honest value is a documented absence, which makes field-requiring experiments decide as DOES_NOT_MEET instead of NEED_MORE_INFORMATION.
core_passport.how_to_document: Value of the installed magnet, optional magnet as optional_not_installed, or install=not_available with evidence when the complete specification/component list shows no magnet.

core_passport.why: Splits the equipment world in two: evacuated sample spaces (cryostats, TVAC, freeze dryers, cryo-FIB, ARPES/UHV, matrix isolation, boil-off calorimeters) versus atmospheric/vapour storage (freezers, dewars, microtomes, climatic chambers, Charpy baths). Many procedures (GEVS TVAC, lyophilisation, ice analogues, ARPES) require it; many others forbid it.
core_passport.how_to_document: Flag b=true/false with a source that describes the sample space (e.g. 'shroud ... vacuum ATM to 1e-7 Torr' or 'vapour-phase storage at atmospheric pressure').

core_passport.why: Quantifies the vacuum: GEVS asks for < 1.33e-3 Pa, freeze-drying runs at 10-30 Pa (or ~13 Pa = 100 mTorr), UHV ice analogue / ARPES work needs ~1e-8 Pa. Machines without vacuum document a sourced absence (not_available), which decides vacuum-requiring experiments.
core_passport.how_to_document: Ultimate/base pressure of the sample space. Torr and mbar convert exactly (Torr = 101325/760 Pa).

core_passport.why: Needed by every spectroscopy, microscopy, photonics, laser, detector, solar-simulation and visual-inspection experiment; trivially documentable (windows/viewports/door window or none).
core_passport.how_to_document: true when a window/viewport onto the sample is part of the documented configuration (an observation window in a freezer/freeze-dryer door counts only if it views the sample space).

core_passport.why: Any powered/biased/measured device under test (DUT in TVAC or climatic chamber, transport sample, detector, qubit, battery cell, HTS tape) needs feedthroughs; storage equipment usually has none, or only a sensor access port.
core_passport.how_to_document: true only when wiring/feedthroughs to the sample are documented; a temperature-probe access port alone is not sample wiring.

core_passport.why: Universal size gate: wafer diameter (51/150/200/300 mm), vial/straw/can/box footprint, puck/bore, test-article envelope in a TVAC chamber, cryo-EM grid/carrier (3 mm), HPF carrier (6 mm). Existing sample.width.max/length.max are documented on only 3 and 1 of 26 configurations and caused NEED_MORE_INFORMATION; one lateral clear dimension is documentable for every machine.
core_passport.how_to_document: Clear diameter of the usable sample space perpendicular to the loading direction; for a rectangular space use the SMALLER of the two documented cross-section dimensions (the quote must contain it). Experiments state the diameter of the circle that circumscribes their sample footprint (conservative).

core_passport.why: Second universal size gate (usable depth along the loading axis): freezer/dewar inside height, rack height, TVAC chamber length, puck/stage clearance, shelf spacing of a freeze dryer.
core_passport.how_to_document: Usable length of the sample space along the loading/insertion axis (vertical for top-/bottom-loading cryostats, freezers, dewars; horizontal depth for front-loading chambers).

core_passport.why: Documented on all 26 existing configurations; every machine either runs on electricity alone (closed-cycle, mechanical cascade, Stirling) or consumes a liquid cryogen. Field, space, MRI-siting, defense and helium-shortage experiments state it as a requirement.
core_passport.how_to_document: true when no liquid cryogen supply is needed in operation (a sealed, factory-filled inventory such as a 7 L sealed MRI magnet still counts as cryogen-free operation only if the source says no refills are needed).

core_passport.why: Already in the vocabulary but never filled. A set of the liquid cryogens the machine uses/holds lets bath and immersion procedures decide: ASTM E1450 needs liquid_helium, Charpy at -196 C / IEC 61788-26 / BS 6364-type valve tests need liquid_nitrogen, cryo-EM plunge freezing needs liquid_ethane (cooled by liquid_nitrogen), LH2 materials tests need liquid_hydrogen, ProtoDUNE needs liquid_argon. A purely mechanical/closed-cycle machine documents the empty set [] (decides any set_contains requirement as not met).
core_passport.how_to_document: Use only these tokens: liquid_nitrogen, liquid_helium, liquid_argon, liquid_hydrogen, liquid_oxygen, liquid_neon, lng, liquid_ethane, dry_ice, compressed_argon_jt (Joule-Thomson cryoprobes), compressed_helium_jt. Empty list = no liquid cryogen.

passport_rules: Every new equipment configuration documents ALL core-passport keys: a value, or install=not_available with a trusted source that shows the absence (complete spec sheet / component list), or optional_not_installed for an option that exists but is not fitted.

Experiment profiles write mandatory requirements on passport keys whenever the physics allows; family keys are added only when the procedure truly needs them (e.g. condenser temperature for lyophilisation).
Never write a mandatory requirement on a key that no machine family documents; check the family_mapping first.

passport_excluded.reason: Not documentable for passive storage dewars and dry shippers (they have no cool-down specification, only a charge/hold time) and rarely a mandatory experiment requirement; keep as a family key for cryostats, cryocoolers, freezers (pull-down time) and TVAC.

Every family rates cooling power at a different temperature (20 mK, 100 mK, 4.2 K, 77 K, 80 K) and storage/thermal-test equipment does not rate it at all; a single passport cooling-power key would be unknown for most machines. Use the temperature-specific family keys (existing at_20mK ... at_20000mK plus the new at_77000mK and at_80000mK).
Freezers document uniformity/stability, dewars and dry shippers do not; useful family key, not universal.

Documented on only 3/1 of 26 existing configurations; superseded for new work by the two universal size keys sample.diameter.max and sample.height.max (existing profiles that use width/length remain valid).

new_keys.description: Usable internal volume of the sample/storage/test space (freezer cabinet, controlled-rate-freezer chamber, environmental or thermal-vacuum chamber, freeze-dryer product chamber, cold room/archive freezer).
Documented maximum number of 1.2/2.0 mL cryovials the storage space holds with the standard inventory system (LN2 freezers, dewars, controlled-rate freezers, ULT freezers when stated in vials).
Documented maximum number of 0.5 mL (1/2 cc) straws the storage/shipping vessel holds (semen and embryo banking, IVF, livestock genetics).

Documented static holding time: how long one cryogen charge keeps the storage/sample space at its rated temperature without refill and without external power (LN2 dewars, vapour freezers, dry shippers, LHe cryostats). Days convert exactly (1 d = 24 h).

documentable_example.value_as_printed: STATIC HOLD TIME (EXCLUDING INVENTORY) 18 DAYS (MVE dry shipper)

new_keys.description: Temperature range of the thermal shroud / cold wall that surrounds the test article in a thermal-vacuum or space-simulation chamber (the radiative environment; the platen/test-article interface range is temperature.range).

documentable_example.value_as_printed: Shroud temperature control range: -180 to +150 C

new_keys.description: Lowest documented temperature of the ice condenser / cold trap of a freeze dryer or cryogenic trap (decides aqueous (-50 C) versus solvent/low-collapse (-80 to -85 C) lyophilisation).

new_keys.description: Documented maximum ice load of the freeze-dryer condenser before defrost, in kg (capacities printed in litres are a different dimension and must NOT be converted).

new_keys.description: Range of controlled (programmable) cooling rates the machine can impose on the sample, as magnitudes (controlled-rate freezers, cryo-stages, DSC, climatic chambers). point_within checks protocols such as -1 C/min cell freezing or 0.3 C/min slow embryo freezing; existing temperature.cooling_rate.max only bounds the fast end.

documentable_example.value_as_printed: Cooling Rates -0.01 C/min to -50 C/min (Planer Kryo 560)

new_keys.description: Documented cooling power (lift) at 77 K (tactical IR Stirling coolers, HTS cable/SFCL coolers, LNG/LN2 reliquefiers). Record the ambient/reject condition in the evidence.
Documented cooling power at 80 K (the standard rating point of space and long-life pulse-tube/Stirling coolers for IR focal planes).

documentable_example.value_as_printed: nominal cooling capacity of 7 W at 80 K with 400 W input power (NICMOS cryocooler)

new_keys.description: Maximum allowable working pressure of the sample vessel/chamber/flow loop (cryogenic test vessels, supercritical-helium loops, high-pressure freezers, hydrate cells, LH2/LNG tanks). bar converts exactly (1 bar = 100000 Pa); psi has no terminating-decimal Pa value, so a psi rating can only be stored as a lower bound rounded DOWN with the printed value kept in the quote.

new_keys.description: Maximum flow of LIQUID cryogen the machine can deliver to the process or meter under test (cryogenic machining nozzles, LN2 tunnel freezers, LNG/LN2 flow-calibration rigs, transfer systems). Gas flow stays in gas.flow_rate.max. m3/h values convert exactly only when divisible by 3 (1 m3/h = 50/3 L/min); otherwise store a value rounded DOWN and keep the printed value in the quote.

new_keys.description: Maximum transport current of the installed current leads/power circuit to the sample (HTS tape and cable critical-current tests, magnet and fusion-conductor tests). Different from electrical.current.max, which is the excitation current of a measurement module.

new_keys.description: Controllable relative-humidity range of the sample chamber (cryo-EM plunge freezers, climatic/damp-heat chambers, AIDA-type cloud chambers).

reuse_existing_keys.cooldown_time.max: Pull-down time of freezers, cool-down of TVAC shroud, cryocooler cool-down (e.g. Ricor K508 '5 min typ' to 80 K).
reuse_existing_keys.temperature.gradient: Cabinet/shelf/platen uniformity (e.g. freeze-dryer shelf uniformity, freezer uniformity).
reuse_existing_keys.temperature.sweep_rate.max: Fastest heating/cooling or transition rate of climatic/thermal-shock chambers, temperature forcing systems and TVAC ramps.
reuse_existing_keys.temperature.cooling_rate.max: Fast end of a controlled-rate freezer (kept for existing profiles; new profiles prefer temperature.cooling_rate.range).
reuse_existing_keys.sample.mass.max: Payload capacity of TVAC/space chambers and load capacity of sample holders (lb converts exactly: 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).
reuse_existing_keys.gas.flow_rate.max: Cold-gas streams (Cryostream 5 or 10 L/min N2) and purge flows.
reuse_existing_keys.cryogen.consumption_rate: Static evaporation rate of dewars (L/day -> L/min exactly: divide by 1440, store as exact decimal only if terminating, else round UP for a 'lower is better' key).
reuse_existing_keys.operating_duration.max: Continuous run time when documented (e.g. ADR hold time at 50 mK).
reuse_existing_keys.vibration.max: Stage vibration of probe stations, ion-trap and SNSPD cryostats.
reuse_existing_keys.module.magnetic_shielding: MEG rooms, qubit cans, CCC shields.
reuse_existing_keys.rf.power.max / electrical.coax_lines / e: RF-tested detectors, qubits, LNAs, SRF cavities.
reuse_existing_keys.optical.transmission_range / optical.cle: Spectroscopy, solar simulation through TVAC windows, IR detector test dewars.
reuse_existing_keys.electrical.dc_lines / electrical.probe_a: Feedthrough counts in TVAC/climatic chambers and probe stations.
reuse_existing_keys.cooling_power.at_20000mK: LH2-temperature lift (SPARC 600 W at 20 K helium system, LH2 zero-boil-off coolers).
reuse_existing_keys.cooling_power.at_4200mK: MEG/MRI reliquefiers, PJVS cryocoolers (0.5 W at 4 K needed), ion-trap cryostats.

unit_rules: Fahrenheit -> mK exactly only when (F - 32) x 5/9 gives a terminating decimal; otherwise store the bound rounded toward the LESS capable side and keep the printed value in the quote.
Torr -> Pa is exact in the unit system (use unit 'Torr' directly); mTorr = '0.001' Torr.
bar -> Pa exactly (x 100000); psi is NOT a registered unit and has no terminating Pa value: store a capability rounded DOWN (requirement rounded UP) and keep the printed psi in the quote.
m3/h -> L_per_min exactly only if divisible by 3; otherwise round in the safe direction as above.
lb -> kg exactly (x 0.45359237); ft3 -> L exactly (x 28.316846592); inch is a registered unit.
L/day -> L_per_min: divide by 1440 (store with unit L_per_min only when the quotient terminates; otherwise round toward the less capable side).
Values are integers or exact decimal strings, never floats.
